title: Regularity of finite simultaneous roots along strict normal crossings
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring such that $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, $r\geq0$, be equations of the pairwise distinct reduced irreducible branches of a strict normal crossings boundary on $X$, with these branches precisely the closed subschemes $V(t_i)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $n\geq1$ be an integer whose image $n\cdot1_A$ is a unit. Then the ring $$C_n=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),$$ formed using multivariate polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], is a regular Noetherian ring: each prime localization of $C_n$ is a regular local ring. The zero ring and the empty boundary are permitted; when $r=0$, $C_n=A$.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, simultaneous parameter-root algebra before invariants. Regularity of the full covering algebra on a regular SNC pair, including the loci where some branch equations are units; the branch-parameter criterion is Stacks Tag 0BIA (etale-lemma-strict-normal-crossings), literature/stacks-project/etale.tex.

proof.text: The regular scheme $X$ is locally Noetherian by [def-weil-regular-scheme], so its affine coordinate ring $A$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. The displayed finite polynomial presentation of $C_n$ then makes $C_n$ Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. If $A=0$, this quotient is zero and has no prime ideals. Otherwise fix an arbitrary prime $q\subset C_n$, let $p=q\cap A$, and put $R=A_p=\mathcal O_{X,p}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. It suffices to show that the localization of the same root presentation over $R$ at the prime induced by $q$ is regular local.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133: full parameter-root algebra before invariants; the induction below supplies the regularity argument left implicit there.

proof.text: Write $I=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, $S=\{i\in I:t_i\in p\}$ and $d=\dim R$. For $J\subseteq S$ put $R_J=R/(t_j:j\in J)$. The intersection of the branches indexed by $J$ is the affine closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(t_j:j\in J))$ and contains $p$. By [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] its local ring there is regular local, and its dimension plus $|J|$ is $d$. The quotient-localization isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], together with [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], identifies this local ring with $R_J$, preserving the images of the $t_i$. Thus each $R_J$ is regular local with $\dim R_J+|J|=d$. If $i\notin S$, $t_i$ is already a unit in $R$, hence also in every $R_J$.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), regular-intersection criterion and its proof; the required dimension equality is explicitly included in the boundary definition used here.

proof.text: For disjoint $J\subseteq S$ and $K\subseteq I\setminus J$, set $B_{J,K}=R_J[x_i:i\in K]/(x_i^n-t_i:i\in K)$. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives a finite free $R_J$-basis $\prod_{i\in K}x_i^{a_i}$, $0\leq a_i<n$. The presentation can be iterated in any order: the maps in both directions fix constants and send each root coordinate to the coordinate with the same index; their composites fix all algebra generators. In particular all these rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. We prove simultaneously for all $J$ that $B_{J,K}$ is regular, by induction on $|K|$. For $K=\varnothing$ it is $R_J$, which is a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. This formulation allows the induction hypothesis to be applied with $J$ enlarged when a root coordinate is killed.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133: full parameter-root algebra before invariants; the induction below supplies the regularity argument left implicit there.

proof.text: For the induction step choose $i\in K$, put $K'=K\setminus\{i\}$ and $D=B_{J,K'}$. The induction hypothesis makes $D$ regular. Set $B=D[T]/(T^n-t_i)$ and write $u$ for the class of $T$; this is $B_{J,K}$. Fix a prime $Q\subset B$ containing $u$. The relation $u^n=t_i$ implies that $i\in S$, since otherwise $t_i$, and hence $u$, would be a unit. In $R_J$, $t_i\ne0$: otherwise $R_{J\cup\{i\}}=R_J$, contradicting the two dimension equalities from step 2. Since $R_J$ is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], multiplication by $t_i$ is injective on $R_J$ and therefore on $D$, coordinate by coordinate in the free basis of step 3.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133: full parameter-root algebra before invariants; the induction below supplies the regularity argument left implicit there.

proof.text: Reduction of the monic presentations modulo $t_i$ identifies $D/(t_i)$ with $B_{J\cup\{i\},K'}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. Explicitly the map sends each coefficient in $R_J$ to its class in $R_{J\cup\{i\}}$ and fixes the root coordinates; the inverse sends these classes and roots to their classes in $D/(t_i)$. The relations in both presentations are the same, so both composites fix their generators. This ring is regular by the induction hypothesis with $|K'|<|K|$. Now $D$ is Noetherian, multiplication by $t_i$ on $D$ is injective, $n>0$, and $Q$ contains the root. Thus [lem-sbc-root-algebra-regular-at-root] applies with base $D$ and equation $t_i$, and gives that $B_Q$ is regular local.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133: full parameter-root algebra before invariants; the induction below supplies the regularity argument left implicit there.

proof.text: It remains to treat a prime $Q\subset B$ not containing $u$. Then $t_i=u^n\notin Q$. Put $E=D[1/t_i]$, a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]; its polynomial ring $E[T]$ is regular by [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base]. The derivative of $F=T^n-t_i$ is $nT^{n-1}$. In $E[T]/(F)$ the coordinate $T$ is a unit, with inverse $T^{n-1}/t_i$, and $n$ is a unit as the image of the given unit of $A$. Therefore the derivative has unit image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular] to the derivation $\partial/\partial T$ to obtain regularity of $E[T]/(F)$. The prime $Q$ extends to this ring, since it misses $t_i$; its prime localization is $B_Q$. Indeed each newly inverted $t_i$ is already a unit in $B_Q$, so the maps in both directions are the maps on fractions fixing $D$ and $u$. Hence $B_Q$ is regular local. Together with step 5 this proves the induction step for every prime of $B$.

source.place: Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular), applied to the ordinary polynomial derivative after inverting the branch equation.

proof.text: Apply the completed induction with $J=\varnothing$ and $K=I$. This proves regularity of $R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. This ring is $(A\setminus p)^{-1}C_n$: the isomorphism sends $a/s$ to the localized coefficient $a/s$ and each $x_i$ to its localized class; the inverse evaluates polynomials in those fractions, and the defining relations vanish in both directions. As $A\setminus p$ maps outside $q$, localizing further at the prime induced by $q$ gives exactly $(C_n)_q$ (the two maps on fractions fix $C_n$ and invert all its elements outside $q$). Thus every prime localization of the Noetherian ring $C_n$ is regular local, which is regularity as defined in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For $r=0$ the empty presentation is $A$, and the induction is its base case; $n=1$ is allowed throughout.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q08-e41a9107a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's 7-step proof and every cited statement. Source checked: ILO IX Prop 2.1 proof, printed p.133, which uses the full root algebra A[x]/(x_i^n-t_i) and leaves its regularity implicit. The statement is unchanged and true. Edge cases checked: A=0, r=0, n=1, k[s] and k[s,u]. Repeated branches are excluded, and that hypothesis is needed (k[x,y]/(x^n-y^n) is singular). The induction is set up properly: B_{J,K} for disjoint J⊆S, K⊆I∖J, by induction on |K|, with base R_J regular local by the SNC dimension clauses and 00CT/stalk identification. Step 4: t_i≠0 in R_J follows from the two dimension equalities; R_J is a domain, so t_i is injective on the free D. Step 5: D/(t_i)=B_{J∪{i},K'}, and the root-at-divisor lemma applies with all four hypotheses verified (the lemma itself re-derived via 00NU). Step 6: D[1/t_i] regular, E[T] regular, and ∂F=nT^{n-1} is a unit because T is invertible and n is a unit; then 07PF applies. Step 7 is a valid localization identification. The five declared tool_uses are generic algebra and are accepted. Batch-5: lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base is a Mathlib leaf (MvPolynomial.isRegularRing_of_isRegularRing) with no proof_deps; neither batch-5 assumption gives it and it is not part of either proof, so it is accepted. No duplicates: lem-per-snc-root-algebra-structure is only the strictly henselian local case. No new nodes, no SGA, no fixes.
